assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Fix any real number x. Let m = floor(x). By lem_floor_interval, we have x < m + 1, with m = floor(x). Then lem_subtract_strict applied to a = x and c = m gives x - m < 1. Replacing m by floor(x) yields x - floor(x) < 1. Since x was arbitrary, the result holds for all real x.

steps.derives: Apply lem_floor_interval to an arbitrary real x, with m = floor(x), to get x < floor(x) + 1.
Apply lem_subtract_strict with a = x and c = floor(x) to deduce x - floor(x) < 1.
Because x was arbitrary, conclude that x - floor(x) < 1 holds for every real number x.

lemmas.proof_nl: Fix an arbitrary real number x and let m = floor(x). By the defining property of the floor function, m is an integer with m <= x, and it is the greatest integer with that property. Therefore x cannot be at least m + 1, because if x >= m + 1 then m + 1 would also be an integer less than or equal to x, contradicting the maximality of m. Hence x < m + 1. Combining this with m <= x gives m <= x < m + 1.
lemmas.role_in_assembly: Supplies the floor bound needed before subtracting m from the upper inequality.
lemmas.self_check_notes: This is the usual defining property of floor: m = floor(x) means m is the greatest integer not exceeding x, so m <= x and x < m + 1.

lemmas.proof_nl: Let a and c be real numbers and assume a < c + 1. Subtract c from both sides of the strict inequality. Since adding or subtracting the same real number preserves strict inequalities, we obtain a - c < (c + 1) - c. The right-hand side simplifies to 1, so a - c < 1.
lemmas.role_in_assembly: Converts the upper bound x < floor(x) + 1 into the desired form x - floor(x) < 1.
lemmas.self_check_notes: This is a routine order-preserving subtraction step for strict inequalities over the reals.
